# Tutorials

The tutorials teach Starsim through one example: a simplified measles outbreak in a town, which gains a latent period, age groups, vaccination, other towns, data to fit it to, and more. Each takes 10 to 20 minutes, starts with the model so far (so you can start at any one), and ends with exercises. The [user guide](user_guide.qmd) covers each topic in full.

Most tutorials run models as compartments (groups of people, by state and by age or place), which Starsim runs as equations, as stochastic models, or as agents. Each also shows what changes as agents, one simulated person at a time, for when people differ in ways compartments can't hold.

::: {.grid}
::: {.g-col-6}
[**T1 – Getting started**](tutorials/t1_intro.qmd)

A measles outbreak as an SIR model: run it, plot it, check what Starsim built, and run it as agents.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T2 – Building a model**](tutorials/t2_model.qmd)

The first model in more depth: states, transitions, parameters, time, and results.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T3 – Building a disease**](tutorials/t3_disease.qmd)

A latent period, how long people stay in each state, waning immunity, and deaths; and, as agents, chance and superspreading.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T4 – Mixing**](tutorials/t4_mixing.qmd)

Who meets whom: age groups and contact matrices, movement between towns, and networks of contacts between people.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T5 – Interventions and scenarios**](tutorials/t5_interventions.qmd)

Vaccination, isolating cases, and comparing scenarios across many runs; and, as agents, treatment, screening, and partner notification.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T6 – Data and calibration**](tutorials/t6_data.qmd)

Real places and populations, births and deaths, and fitting the model to reported cases to project a campaign.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T7 – Stratification and co-transmission**](tutorials/t7_strata.qmd)

Splitting a model by more than age, and two diseases that affect each other.
:::

::: {.g-col-6}
[**T8 – Custom modules**](tutorials/t8_modules.qmd)

Writing your own behavior as code: an intervention for compartments, and a disease, a quantity for each person, and a network for agents.
:::

:::

The answers to the exercises are in the [solutions](tutorials/solutions.qmd).

::: {.callout-tip}
## Running tutorials locally

Each tutorial can be downloaded as a Jupyter notebook: look for the download button at the top of the page. Or, to run them all locally: clone the Starsim repository, install Starsim (`pip install -e .`), go to `docs/tutorials`, and open them in Jupyter (`jupyter lab`, with `jupytext` installed to open `.qmd` files directly, or run `./convert_notebooks` first).
:::
